summary: Windsor sits in the heart of Sonoma County's wine country, but the town itself runs on something more practical than Pinot Noir — at 7.5 square miles and roughly 25,700 people, it functions largely as a bedroom community feeding commuters south toward Santa Rosa and beyond, with no major corporate campus or hospital system anchoring local employment. The Russian River winds along its western edge, and the surrounding terrain is classic northern Sonoma: flat valley floor ringed by oak-studded hills that catch golden light on 71°F average highs and nine hours of daily sunshine. A median household income of $129,000 against a median home price of $763,200 yields a price-to-income ratio just under 6:1 — stretched but not as punishing as coastal Bay Area towns, though median rent at $2,087 still absorbs a meaningful share of a middle-income paycheck. The town green and adjacent shops along Old Redwood Highway give Windsor a compact civic center, but the broader layout is subdivision-oriented, requiring a car to connect daily errands. Property crime registers at about 721 per 100K, mostly larceny, while violent crime sits well below state averages and the homicide rate is zero. Windsor is essentially a Sonoma County address at a Sonoma County price, offering vineyard-adjacent calm in exchange for accepting that most of your economic and cultural life will happen somewhere else.
